name: Glassen Reach
geological_features: Vast fused-glass plains stretching thousands of kilometers
Deep radial fracture canyons emanating from a central impact basin
Vitrified mountain ridges with prismatic light refraction
specific_features: The Pane — a single unbroken glass plain visible from orbit, 1,200 km across
Cataclysm shadows: dark silhouettes baked permanently into the glass surface
Subsurface hollow chambers where flash-vaporized material left voids
description: Glassen Reach is a world defined by absence — the absence of whatever stood here before the cataclysm reduced its surface to a planet-wide sheet of fused glass. The terrain is eerily flat across entire hemispheres, broken only by fracture canyons where tectonic stress has cracked the vitrified crust into jagged ravines hundreds of meters deep.

A thin atmosphere clings to the surface, barely enough to carry sound but sufficient to produce a low, constant harmonic hum as wind passes over the glass ridges. At dawn and dusk, the prismatic mountains scatter light into spectral bands that paint the sky in colors no breathable world could replicate.

Orbital scans reveal that the glass plains formed in a single event — not gradual volcanism, but an instantaneous release of energy so catastrophic it liquefied the upper mantle across an entire hemisphere. Whatever civilization or natural force caused this left no other trace, only the dark cataclysm shadows baked into the surface like the afterimages of a forgotten world.

Survey teams report that the subsurface voids contain unusual crystalline formations that defy standard geological models, suggesting the cataclysm may have involved exotic energy sources. Several corporate expeditions have been quietly funded to extract samples, though the brittle glass surface makes landing hazardous and more than one ship has been lost to collapse.
